chapter: Band personalities, Duke's last years and the office
title: Bob Udkoff and the night after Duke died
summary: Udkoff gathered old bandsmen to play Duke's records, taping a Tizol tune for them.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: You ever been to Bob's place?
Udkoff's?
Bob Yutak's? Yeah. Not the one he has now.
The building he built.
Oh, the new one in Westwood? No, I haven't been there; I was to his old place.

Yeah, and the night that Duke died, or the night after Duke died, Bob Yutak had quite a few people over, and everybody that was in Los Angeles who used to be in Duke's band, he had up to his house, and played Duke's records and so forth and so on, and he played a record with a couple of Juan's tunes that I had never heard, and I asked him if he would make a tape of it, and he said yes, and he did make a tape and sent it to us.
Udkoff
And we stayed there until twelve or one o'clock
that night, didn't we Juan? And he was very sad, because you know, he was very much for Duke, very fond of Duke.
Oh, he went everywhere with Duke.
Yeah, he left home, right?
He went to Russia, he went to Rome -- he went everywhere.
Well, he left home when he was 16.
And followed the band.
Uh huh.
You know, his father used to clean the uniforms for the band in New York.
Yeah, Bob told me about that.
And he was 16 years old when he met the band, working in his father's cleaning store. And when the band left town, he couldn't stand it, so he left with them -- ran away.
And you know the funny part about it? He was going to the same dentist here in Beverly Hills that I used to go to.
Juan went to the dentist one day and who comes in but Bob Udakoff.
